newsitem.title: INDIA: India call rates ease, gilt market awaits auction.
newsitem.headline: India call rates ease, gilt market awaits auction.

text.p: Indian call money rates ended lower at 2.50-3.50 percent on Monday against the opening levels of 4.25-5.00 percent, dealers said.
Most of the deals were at 3.50-4.50 percent, with some stray deals at 2.50 percent, they said.

"Call rates are likely to firm up on Wednesday, despite the lower subscription at the latest repo auction, as the advance tax payments and the outflow on June 18 towards the seven-year 20 billion rupees bond auction will affect liqudity," a state-run bank dealer said.
The Reserve Bank of India said on Monday it had accepted five bids for 11 billion rupees at Monday's repo auction.
Easy call levels pushed the interbank term money market today, a dealer at Andhra Bank said.
"We have done a deals in the region of 11.00-11.25 percent for six month maturity," he said.
One month term money was quoted at 5.50/6.50 percent, two months at 9.00/9.50 percent, three months at 10.00/10.50 percent and six month money was quoted at 10.75/11.25 percent.
The demand for securities remained subdued on Monday, a dealer said. "Market seems to be keeping a watch on the Tuesday's seven- year government bond auction," he said.
Market expect the cut-off yield in the region of 12.60-12.65 percent, he added.

Prices on securities hardly moved, a dealer with brokers said. The 12.50 percent government stock 2004 outperformed other stocks. It rose to 99.81 rupees against the previous close of 99.65 rupees, he said.
